question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [French Governor-General / Director — his base of operations in India]
options: Joseph François Dupleix — Pondicherry (served as Governor-General of French India 1742–1754)
Bertrand-François Mahé de La Bourdonnais — Mauritius (Île de France), from where he sailed to capture Madras in 1746
Count de Lally (Thomas Arthur de Lally) — Pondicherry (directed the siege of Madras in 1758–59 and was besieged at Pondicherry in 1760–61)
Charles de Bussy-Castelnau — Calcutta; he controlled Bengal on behalf of the French from 1748 to 1758
wrong_fact: Bussy-Castelnau was NOT based in Calcutta and did NOT control Bengal for France. He operated in the Deccan — specifically at the court of the Nizam of Hyderabad and in the Northern Circars on the Andhra coast. His area of influence was the Deccan and the eastern Andhra coast, not Bengal or Calcutta.
explanation: Charles de Bussy-Castelnau was Dupleix's most capable military lieutenant. He was stationed at Hyderabad's court from around 1751 and secured French influence over the Nizam and the Northern Circars. He was recalled to Pondicherry by Lally in 1758, which was considered a strategic blunder that weakened French influence in the Deccan. Calcutta and Bengal remained a British sphere (especially after Plassey, 1757).

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [French territorial / political ambition — the region it targeted in India]
options: Dupleix's strategy of backing Muzaffar Jung for the Nizamship of Hyderabad — aimed at securing French influence over the Deccan and a large revenue base
French support for Chanda Sahib as Nawab of the Carnatic — aimed at controlling the rich Carnatic region and blocking British access to south India
Bussy's presence at the Nizam's court — secured French control over the Northern Circars on the Coromandel Coast north of Madras
French alliance with the Marathas at Poona — Dupleix's primary diplomatic initiative to encircle British possessions in western India
wrong_fact: Dupleix did NOT form a primary diplomatic alliance with the Marathas at Poona. Dupleix's diplomatic strategy focused on the Deccan (supporting Muzaffar Jung as Nizam) and the Carnatic (supporting Chanda Sahib as Nawab). The Marathas were a separate and often unpredictable power; they were not the centerpiece of Dupleix's diplomatic encirclement strategy.
explanation: Dupleix's grand strategy involved: (1) placing Muzaffar Jung on the throne of Hyderabad and (2) making Chanda Sahib the Nawab of Arcot (Carnatic). This would have given France control over a vast swathe of south India from Hyderabad to the Coromandel Coast. The Maratha alliance was not a key feature of Dupleix's plan; the Marathas were ultimately allied with neither Britain nor France in any systematic way during this period.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [French military action — the location / outcome in India]
options: Capture of Madras (Fort St. George) by La Bourdonnais — 1746; Madras restored to Britain by the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748)
Siege of Trichinopoly (Tiruchirappalli) — French-backed Chanda Sahib besieged the town defended by Muhammad Ali and his British allies (1751–1752)
Siege of Madras by Lally — 1758–1759; French siege of Madras lifted after the arrival of British reinforcements and the naval battle of Masulipatnam
Battle of Wandiwash — 22 January 1760; Sir Eyre Coote decisively defeated Lally and captured Bussy, ending French military power in India
wrong_fact: The French siege of Madras (1758–1759) was NOT lifted due to a naval battle at Masulipatnam. It was lifted because a British naval squadron arrived at Madras roads under Vice-Admiral George Pocock, forcing the French fleet under Comte de Conflans to withdraw. The British naval presence cut French supply lines and made the siege untenable. There was no decisive naval battle at Masulipatnam that ended the siege.
explanation: Lally besieged Madras from December 1758 to February 1759. The siege was abandoned when a British fleet under Admiral Pocock arrived, threatening the French fleet and bringing reinforcements. This failure, compounded by the recall of Bussy from the Deccan, severely weakened French India. The final blow came at the Battle of Wandiwash (1760) where Coote defeated Lally and captured Bussy.
